topic: Critical-plane inference for nested Brenier difference-in-differences. Under the published two-group/two-period cyclic-comonotonicity identification assumptions, take four independent samples from C^s, s>=8, uniformly positive densities on the two-dimensional flat torus with uniformly elliptic Brenier potentials. For p=OT(P_C0,P_C1), Pdagger_T1=p#P_T0, and Tdagger=OT(P_T1,Pdagger_T1), prove that a specified order-s positive-normalized periodized-KDE/Monge-Ampere plug-in has a joint fixed-grid Gaussian limit at sqrt(n/log(1/h)); derive the full four-cell nested critical Green covariance including generated-target cross terms; consistently estimate it by adjoint elliptic solves; give simultaneous multiplier ellipses for y-Tdagger(y); and match log(1/h)/n squared risk by a Hellinger-local minimax lower bound. Use the explicit smooth separable torus witness and target the Card-Krueger bivariate employment reanalysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Pulling both transports into treated-post coordinates gives exactly M=(f_T0/f_C0)C for the inner and generated-pushforward elliptic coefficients, reducing the nested derivative to one outer Green response to four weighted noises plus an order-minus-two remainder. This rules out independent-cell cancellation and predicts covariance blocks V_j=w_j sqrt(det DT(y_j))DT(y_j)/(4pi f_T1(y_j)); matrix identities, angular constants, bandwidth feasibility, clipping, and the separable witness were checked, and no collision was found including an August 2026 potential-CLT follow-up. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniformly that the full transformed-KDE variable-coefficient Green response has the stated log-normalized covariance while generated-target and estimated-coefficient/pole remainders are negligible. EARLY KILL TEST: On one nonseparable smooth torus example with nonconstant f_T0/f_C0, compute adjoint covariance increments at h,h/2,h/4,h/8 with resolved discretization error; stop or pivot if logarithmic slopes miss the formula or the remainder diverges logarithmically. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_bivariate_cic_critical_transport_inference.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published smooth-map CLT begins at d = 3, whereas in d = 2 the squared gradient of the elliptic Green function is borderline nonintegrable and produces logarithmic normalization. Nested OT-CiC adds a second obstacle: the control samples estimate an inner map, that map pushes forward the treated-pre law, and the generated law becomes a marginal of the outer map. The same noises therefore reach the final displacement through several correlated paths. Existing linearizations perturb one map or one density curve, while the prior panel review independently warns that omitting analogous generated-object cross terms changes the limit. The missing step is a uniform chain-rule expansion that pulls all responses into treated-post coordinates and controls the variable-coefficient, generated-pushforward, estimated-pole, and nonlinear remainders on the logarithmic scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint fixed-grid central limit theorem at rate sqrt(n/log(1/h_n)) expressing the nested displacement as one outer Green response to four explicitly weighted empirical noises, with a closed-form full covariance matrix and a uniform order-minus-two remainder bound.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Available lower bounds concern one transport map under global integrated loss. A local nested lower bound must instead preserve four positive smooth torus densities, uniform ellipticity, and the cyclic-comonotone causal model while separating a fixed-point functional. The in-repo critical-rate analysis records that a single bump misses the logarithmic factor. Multiscale or annular perturbations must accumulate the Green singularity while keeping product-measure Hellinger distance bounded, and the perturbations must be coordinated across cells so the nested derivative does not cancel their separation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Le Cam or Assouad theorem on an explicit four-sample smooth-torus subexperiment with bounded product Hellinger distance and nested-displacement separation of order sqrt(log(1/h_n)/n), paired with a matching plug-in upper bound.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Green covariance contains unknown coefficient matrices, density weights, evaluation poles, and derivatives of the generated pushforward, all estimated from the same four samples. Consistency of coefficients in a weak norm is insufficient because errors must remain negligible after logarithmic normalization near an h-dependent Green singularity. Existing transport confidence procedures are one-dimensional, regularized, semidiscrete, or concern potential contrasts. The prior conditional-transport proposal also left observed covariance plug-in and common-multiplier calibration unresolved. The first missing proof step is a stable adjoint representation for every covariance block, including off-diagonal generated-target blocks, followed by uniform control of estimated coefficients, clipping, poles, and multiplier covariance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An operator-norm consistent covariance estimator assembled from four collections of estimated adjoint Green influence vectors, plus conditional convergence of a studentized Gaussian-multiplier maximum yielding simultaneous 1-alpha ellipses for all vectors y_j-Tdagger(y_j).

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing emphasizes the practical gap between pointwise estimation and interpretable simultaneous uncertainty for a transport map.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A transport map is a function rather than a scalar -> separate pointwise intervals do not give simultaneous guarantees -> resampling makes transport uncertainty operational -> nested bivariate DiD needs fixed-grid vector ellipses preserving generated-target dependence

method_exemplars.technique: Represent linear functionals through the adjoint of the inverse linearized elliptic operator and establish stability and bootstrap convergence for the resulting influence functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired covariance estimator likewise converts each grid evaluation into an adjoint solve, with new work needed for gradients, critical normalization, and four dependent paths.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply covariance-sensitive Gaussian approximation and multiplier calibration to maxima of stacked cellwise influence-vector sums.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After adjoint influence vectors are established, the ellipse statistic is a maximum of correlated finite-grid vector norms.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its studentization and simultaneous resampling architecture, replacing scalar quantile influence functions with adjoint elliptic responses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest existing coverage result for a transport map, while the bivariate nested problem requires different influence machinery.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The proposed smooth-torus inference model and the motivating application occupy different statistical regimes: full-time and part-time employment are integer-valued with ties and atoms, whereas Brenier-map uniqueness and elliptic linearization require positive continuous densities. Jittering, KDE smoothing, clipping, or torus wrapping selects a regularized map and can alter the causal estimand. Scalar discrete CiC does not extend canonically to vectors, while existing discrete-plan structure results do not impose the cross-period compatibility required to characterize every admissible counterfactual.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-dimensional characterization of the counterfactual treated-post distributions or displacement sets generated by cyclically compatible optimal plans across the four discrete cells, together with a directionally differentiable support-function estimator and an asymptotically valid confidence region.

writing_exemplar.why: It already connects multivariate changes-in-changes to Card-Krueger and explicitly exposes the discrete nonuniqueness boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Employment adjustment is intrinsically bivariate -> multivariate changes-in-changes captures dependence missed by coordinatewise analysis -> observed employment outcomes are discrete so Brenier point identification fails -> report a sharp set of compatible counterfactuals with valid uncertainty

method_exemplars.technique: Use decomposition of discrete optimal plans into deterministic components and infinity-Wasserstein control to parameterize extreme admissible transports.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Extreme transports are natural candidates for deriving endpoints or support functions of the discrete multivariate CiC identified set.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative and use modified resampling valid for nondifferentiable functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Support functions and extrema of a transport-plan polytope are generally only directionally differentiable.

literature_map:
1. Athey and Imbens (2006, Econometrica) identify scalar changes-in-changes counterfactual distributions and treat discrete scalar outcomes.
2. Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024, Journal of Causal Inference; arXiv:2108.05858) identify multivariate changes-in-changes through cyclically comonotone Brenier maps and reanalyze Card-Krueger, but stop at consistency and computation.
3. Hütter and Rigollet (2021, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1905.05828) establish smooth transport-map minimax rates under global loss using stability and information-theoretic lower bounds.
4. Deb, Ghosal, and Sen (2021, NeurIPS; arXiv:2107.01718) show how smoothing improves barycentric transport-map plug-in rates.
5. Manole, Balakrishnan, Niles-Weed, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:2107.12364) prove minimax properties of density plug-ins and CLTs for squared Wasserstein distance, not pointwise nested maps.
6. Manole, Balakrishnan, Niles-Weed, and Wasserman (2023+, arXiv:2312.12407) prove pointwise smooth-map CLTs on a flat torus for d >= 3 through quantitative Monge-Ampère linearization; d = 2 is outside the theorem.
7. González-Sanz and Sheng (2024, arXiv:2408.06534) prove Fréchet differentiability of smooth Brenier maps through the linearized Monge-Ampère equation.
8. Balakrishnan and Manole (2025, arXiv:2502.12326) obtain broader plug-in transport-map stability bounds but do not give critical-plane limit theory.
9. Sadhu, Goldfeld, and Kato (2023+, arXiv:2303.10155) derive limits and bootstrap inference for semidiscrete transport-map functionals.
10. Goldfeld, Kato, Rioux, and Sadhu (2024, Electronic Journal of Statistics; arXiv:2207.08683) use marginal-wise Hadamard differentiability for CLTs and bootstrap inference on entropic transport maps.
11. Ponnoprat, Okano, and Imaizumi (2024, Electronic Journal of Statistics; arXiv:2307.09257) give uniform confidence bands for one-dimensional transport maps using quantile representations.
12. González-Sanz, Sheng, Wu, and Avella Medina (2026, arXiv:2607.19080) identify a gradient-Green pole and infinite-variance empirical influence response in d >= 2.
13. González-Sanz, Mordant, and Sheng (2026, arXiv:2608.00649) use elliptic inverses and adjoints for functional limits and bootstrap inference on empirical Brenier potentials, but not nested pointwise gradients.
14. Auricchio and Veneroni (2022, Applied Mathematics & Optimization; arXiv:2104.13106) characterize discrete optimal plans, supplying machinery for the count-valued application boundary.
15. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1212.6906) provide Gaussian-multiplier approximation tools applicable once valid fixed-grid influence vectors and covariance estimates are available.
